query: answer engine optimization vs generative engine optimization

seo.title: AEO vs GEO: What's the Difference and Which Matters?
seo.meta_description: AEO vs GEO compared: answer engine optimization targets snippets and voice answers, GEO targets AI-written answers. See where they overlap and what to do.

h1: AEO vs GEO: Answer Engine Optimization vs Generative Engine Optimization
answer: In AEO vs GEO, answer engine optimization (AEO) aims to make your content the direct answer in featured snippets, People Also Ask boxes and voice assistants, while generative engine optimization (GEO) aims to get your brand named and cited inside AI-written answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. The tactics overlap heavily, so most businesses should do both.
key_takeaways: AEO grew up around featured snippets, People Also Ask and voice search.
GEO focuses on generative AI assistants that write answers and cite several sources.
Both reward direct answers, question headings, FAQs and structured data.
GEO adds brand-level work: mentions across the web and access for AI crawlers.
Treat AEO as part of GEO rather than a separate program.

sections.heading: What answer engine optimization means
sections.body_html:
Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the practice of structuring content so a search engine or assistant can lift it as the single, direct answer to a question. The term became popular as Google added featured snippets and People Also Ask boxes, and as voice assistants started reading answers aloud.

Classic AEO tactics include answering a question in one clear paragraph, using the question as a heading, adding numbered steps or tables Google can show as a snippet, and marking up content with FAQ or HowTo structured data where appropriate.

sections.heading: What generative engine optimization means
sections.body_html:
Generative engine optimization (GEO) targets AI systems that write an answer rather than quote one. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot and Google's AI Overviews read multiple sources, combine them and present a new response, usually naming brands and linking to a few pages.

The term comes from a 2023 research paper that measured how content changes affect a source's visibility in generated answers. Its best methods, such as adding citations, quotations and statistics, improved visibility by up to 40% in the authors' tests.

sections.heading: AEO vs GEO side by side
sections.body_html:
AEOGEO
Target surfaceFeatured snippets, People Also Ask, voice answersAI-written answers in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, AI Overviews
What winsOne page quoted as the answerSeveral sources summarized; brands named in the answer
Unit of optimizationA concise answer blockPassages across many pages, plus the brand as an entity

MeasurementSnippet ownership, impressions and clicksMentions and citations per engine, AI referral visits, leads

sections.heading: Where AEO and GEO overlap
sections.body_html:
Most of the page-level work is identical. Both approaches reward:

  • A direct answer to the exact question in the first lines.
  • Headings phrased as the questions people ask.
  • Short paragraphs, numbered steps, lists and comparison tables.
  • FAQs that cover the natural follow-up questions.
  • Structured data that matches what is visible on the page.
  • Helpful, accurate content from a source that shows real expertise.

If you have done good AEO work, you already have a head start on GEO.

sections.heading: What GEO adds beyond AEO
sections.body_html:
Brand mentions, not just page answers

Generative engines often answer "which provider should I choose?" by naming companies. Whether you are named depends on what the wider web says about you: reviews, directories, industry articles, community discussions and partner pages. AEO rarely looked beyond your own page.

Access for AI crawlers

AI assistants use their own crawlers alongside search indexes. OpenAI documents OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT search and Perplexity documents PerplexityBot. If they are blocked, those products cannot cite you, no matter how good your answer is.

Evidence density

Because generative engines combine sources, they favor pages that add something specific: a statistic, a quote, a real example, a clear trade-off. A page that only restates the common answer has less reason to be chosen.

Machine-readable maps

Files such as llms.txt give AI tools a clean list of your most useful pages. It is a young proposal and support varies, but it costs little to add.

sections.heading: Which should you prioritize?
sections.body_html:
You do not have to choose. A practical order of work:

  1. Fix the foundations so pages are crawlable and indexed by search engines and AI crawlers.
  2. Apply AEO formatting to your most important pages: direct answers, question headings, FAQs and schema.
  3. Add GEO depth: sourced facts, examples, comparisons and a clear statement of who you serve.
  4. Build off-site signals so AI engines can confidently name your brand.
  5. Measure both: snippet and search performance in Search Console, plus citations and AI referrals.

For a local service business, AEO often wins quick results in voice and snippet answers. For B2B and considered purchases, GEO usually matters more, because buyers ask AI assistants to compare providers.

sections.heading: An example of the same page done for AEO and for GEO
sections.body_html:
Take the question "How much does a GEO audit cost?"

AEO version: a heading with the question, a two-sentence answer explaining what affects the price, and a short list of factors. Good for a featured snippet.

GEO version: everything above, plus a table of what different audit levels include, an explanation of when a cheap audit is enough and when it is not, a real example of findings from an audit, a note on how long it takes, and FAQs on follow-up questions. Good for a snippet, and far more likely to be cited and summarized by an AI assistant that is comparing options for the buyer.

sections.heading: Common misconceptions
sections.body_html:
• "AEO is dead." Snippets and voice answers still exist, and their formatting habits are exactly what generative engines like.
  • "GEO is just SEO with a new name." It shares foundations but adds brand-level signals, AI crawler access and citation-based measurement.
  • "Schema alone will get me into AI answers." Structured data helps engines understand pages, but the content itself still has to be the best answer.
  • "You need different content for each engine." One well-structured, specific page usually serves search, snippets and AI answers at once.

faqs.q: What is the difference between AEO and GEO?
faqs.a: AEO focuses on making your content the direct answer in featured snippets, People Also Ask and voice assistants. GEO focuses on getting your brand named and your pages cited inside AI-written answers from tools such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews.

In practice, yes. The page-level tactics of AEO, such as direct answers, question headings, FAQs and schema, are the foundation of GEO. GEO then adds brand mentions across the web, AI crawler access and deeper evidence.

faqs.q: Which is better for a small business, AEO or GEO?
faqs.a: Local service businesses often see quick AEO wins in snippets and voice answers. Businesses whose buyers compare providers before buying usually gain more from GEO. Most small businesses benefit from doing the shared basics first.

faqs.q: Does structured data help with AEO and GEO?
faqs.a: It helps engines understand what a page is about and can make it eligible for rich results, as long as it matches the visible content. It supports both approaches but does not replace a genuinely useful answer.

faqs.q: How do I measure AEO vs GEO results?
faqs.a: Measure AEO with snippet ownership, impressions and clicks in Google Search Console. Measure GEO by testing a fixed list of questions in each AI engine monthly, tracking mentions and citations, and counting visits and leads from AI referrers.

faqs.q: Will AEO and GEO replace SEO?
faqs.a: No. Both build on SEO foundations such as crawlable, indexed, trustworthy pages. They change how you write and measure, not whether search engines need to find and trust you.
